title: Wheaton College (Wheaton)
summary: Wheaton College (Wheaton) is a university in Wheaton. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with Wheaton.

sections.heading: What Wheaton is known for
paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) is a private nonprofit institution with an undergraduate enrollment of 2,121 students. The college has a relatively high admission rate of 87.4%, reflecting its inclusive admissions approach. Wheaton is known for offering a variety of academic programs, with notable shares in business and health fields. Approximately 11.92% of its programs are focused on business, while about 1.54% are dedicated to health-related studies. These program distributions highlight Wheaton's commitment to providing diverse educational opportunities within a private nonprofit framework.

sections.heading: Key strengths
paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) is a private nonprofit institution recognized for its diverse academic offerings. Among its programs, education accounts for approximately 4.81%, indicating a significant focus on preparing students for careers in teaching and educational fields. Health-related programs represent about 1.54% of the curriculum, reflecting a smaller but notable commitment to health sciences. These program shares demonstrate Wheaton's dedication to providing a range of academic disciplines within its private nonprofit structure.

sections.heading: Popular majors
paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) offers a variety of popular majors, with business programs comprising approximately 11.92% of the academic offerings. Education is another significant area of study, representing about 4.81% of the programs available to students. Computer-related fields account for roughly 3.27%, while health-related programs make up around 1.54% of the curriculum. Public administration is not represented among the popular majors at Wheaton. These distributions illustrate the college's focus on diverse academic disciplines, particularly in business and education.

paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) has an undergraduate admission rate of approximately 87.4%, indicating a relatively accessible admissions process. sections.heading: How to read Wheaton tuition
paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) charges a tuition fee of $45,546 for both in-state and out-of-state students, reflecting a uniform tuition policy regardless of residency. The total cost of attendance, which includes tuition along with additional expenses such as fees, room, board, and other related costs, amounts to $59,263. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and families plan for the financial commitment required to attend Wheaton.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) offers financial aid to support students in managing the cost of attendance. Approximately 21.71% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies aimed at assisting low-income students. Among those who complete their studies, the median debt incurred is $23,250, indicating the typical loan amount graduates carry. Prospective students can explore detailed financial aid information and use the net price calculator available on Wheaton's official website at www.wheaton.edu/. Additional data on costs and aid can also be found through the College Scorecard at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?149781.

sections.heading: Colleges and schools
paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) does not have distinct colleges or schools within its academic structure. Instead, it offers a range of undergraduate programs across various disciplines. The institution emphasizes a comprehensive liberal arts education, integrating faith and learning in its curriculum. Students at Wheaton engage in diverse fields of study, supported by faculty committed to academic excellence and spiritual growth.

sections.heading: Academic features
paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) maintains a student-faculty ratio of 10, fostering an environment conducive to personalized instruction and close interaction between students and professors. This ratio supports Wheaton's commitment to providing a rigorous liberal arts education, allowing for meaningful academic engagement and mentorship. The institution's academic features emphasize a balance between intellectual development and spiritual formation, aligning with its broader educational mission.

paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) primarily offers undergraduate degree programs, focusing on a comprehensive liberal arts education. The institution does not have separate colleges or schools but provides a variety of academic disciplines within its undergraduate curriculum. Wheaton emphasizes personalized instruction, supported by a low student-faculty ratio, to foster close interaction and mentorship. sections.heading: Housing and dining
paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) provides housing options for students both on and off campus, with associated room and board costs reflecting these choices. The estimated annual expense for living on campus, including room and board, is $13,010. For students who choose to live off campus, the combined cost of room and board is slightly lower, at $12,868. These figures help students and families consider the financial aspects of housing while planning for their education at Wheaton.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) reports a completion rate of approximately 84.75% within 150% of the expected time, indicating that a significant majority of students finish their programs. Graduates experience median earnings of $50,270 six years after enrollment, which increase to $63,756 when measured ten years post-enrollment. These figures suggest positive long-term career outcomes for Wheaton alumni. Among those who complete their studies, the median student debt is $23,250, reflecting the typical financial obligation carried by graduates. These data points provide insight into the career and financial trajectories of students who attend Wheaton.

paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) offers opportunities for students to engage in internships and research as part of their academic experience. sections.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: Wheaton College (Wheaton) exhibits a diverse student body with a gender distribution of approximately 45.73% men and 54.27% women. The racial composition includes about 67.23% White students, 3.25% Black students, 8.72% Hispanic students, and 8.82% Asian students. These figures reflect Wheaton's commitment to fostering an inclusive campus environment. Additionally, around 21.71% of the student population receives Pell Grants, indicating a significant portion of students benefit from federal financial aid aimed at supporting those with financial need.

The college provides a liberal arts environment that may appeal to those seeking a broad-based education alongside their technical coursework.
